 Follow Texas man identified as pilot in Sandusky County plane crash
 Andrew Bailey Updated Fri, November 13, 2026 at 5:35 PM UTC 1 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. The pilot of a plane that crash-landed into a field in Sandusky County Thursday afternoon has been identified.
 Clifton Green, 64, of Fort Worth, Texas, suffered serious injuries in the crash and was taken to the hospital, the Ohio State Highway Patrol said in a press release on Friday. Further details about Green's condition are not known at this time.
 Green was flying a 1965 Moonie M20C single-engine plane northward to Michigan when it began to have mechanical issues. OSHP did not give further details about what caused the crash, which happened at 2:35 p.m. in a field by the U.S. 20 and U.S. 23 intersection, just northwest of Woodville.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Jet fuel also spilled from the plane into the field, and the Environmental Protection Agency was contacted about it, OSHP.
 Woodville's assistant fire chief, Mark Grove, said an airboat from Ballville Township, just outside Fremont, assisted with removing the plane from the scene due to the ground being too muddy from rain for trucks and other vehicles to go out there.
 Utah-based TSS Glass Machinery Sales has confirmed it owns the plane. Green is the company's founder and president, according to his LinkedIn.
 The Federal Aviation Administration and the National Traffic Safety Board are assisting OSHP, the lead investigating agency, with the investigation.
